precepts.text: The Lord also shall save the tents of Judah first. That is what the white man knows: it is not Judah over in Africa, it is not Judah in Saudi Arabia; it is Judah here, and the Lord is going to raise them up first.
precepts.point: Back to the hearings: "Within the Negro population of the United States the Negro working class is destined to be the vanguard of all liberation movements, and may become the vanguard of the liberation movement of the Negro peasant masses on an international scale. A strong Negro movement in the USA will be able to influence and direct the Negro movement in all those backward parts of the world where the Negroes are oppressed by the various imperialist powers." You see what they called all the other places: backward parts of the earth. That is why Esau always has his eye on the American blacks. People ask why Canada and Europe have free healthcare and not America: they do not want the American blacks to get it, because this group here is more dangerous than all the other groups. Sisters, do not just let your boys run out; the white man has his eyes on your sons; they know what stock they come from.

note.label: We Are Born in Babylon

precepts.why:
Nebuchadnezzar told Ashpenaz to bring “certain of the children of Israel, and of the king’s seed, and of the princes; Children in whom was no blemish, but well favoured, and skilful in all wisdom, and cunning in knowledge, and understanding science”. That is what Deacon Malachi was talking about: Babylon didn't take any old body. Esau did the same thing. They said no, we need the best ones, and put them in North America. The ones they left behind were not the same, and that is why you see Africa the way it is.

The hearings they read say it: within the Negro population of the United States, the Negro working class is destined to be the vanguard of all liberation movements, and a strong Negro movement in the USA will be able to influence and direct the Negro movement in all those backward parts of the world. See what they called all the other places: backward parts of the earth. That is why Esau always has his eye on the American blacks. Canada and Europe have free healthcare and America does not, because they don't want the American blacks to get it; this group here is more dangerous than all the other groups.

That is why the Lord said: “The Lord also shall save the tents of Judah first”. That is what the white man knows. It isn't Judah over in Africa; it isn't Judah in Saudi Arabia. It's Judah here, and the Lord is going to raise them up first.

So be proud of this history. Don't be mad; be glad. Sisters, don't just let your boys run out: the white man has his eyes on your sons, because they know what stock they come from. Even if the father was no good, the son is still of good stock, and there is still hope for him.

precepts.text: Here's a prophecy: the Lord also shall save the tents of Judah first. So when Christ came, he wasn't going, hey, I'm just gathering all Israel. He said, no, I got to start with Judah, and then the rest of them come later on.
precepts.point: Pay attention. Go not into the way of the Gentiles, and into any city of the Samaritans enter ye not: those Gentiles there is the northern kingdom. That's why they're in the same sentence with Samaria. Why does he stipulate the Samaritans? That was the leading tribe, Ephraim. But go rather to the lost sheep of the house of Israel: meaning the kingdom of Judah. Start with Judah first.

note.label: Raising Up the Tabernacle of David That Fell

precepts.why:
Christ commanded the twelve, “Go not into the way of the Gentiles, and into any city of the Samaritans enter ye not: But go rather to the lost sheep of the house of Israel.” Those Gentiles are the northern kingdom; that's why they are in the same sentence with Samaria. He names the Samaritans because Ephraim was the leading tribe. The lost sheep there means the kingdom of Judah: start with Judah first.

Here's the prophecy of it: “The Lord also shall save the tents of Judah first, that the glory of the house of David and the glory of the inhabitants of Jerusalem do not magnify themselves against Judah.” The tents of Judah first.

So when Christ came, he wasn't going, hey, I'm just gathering all Israel at once. He said, no, I got to start with Judah, and then the rest of them come later on. That is why he held the apostles back from the Gentiles and the Samaritans in Matthew 10: the order was set by the prophet, Judah first.

precepts.text: The Lord also shall save the tents of Judah first: God is going to raise up the tribe of Judah first, Judah in America, and then Judah will know where God's people is and go find them.
precepts.point: The revised twelve tribe chart was shown in class: Judah includes American blacks and the Igbo of Nigeria; the chart now carries tribes identified across Africa, India, and the islands, from the Falasha of Ethiopia to the Kikuyu of Kenya to the Sefwi Israelites of Ghana, the Fon and Ashanti under Benjamin, the Zulu under Simeon, the Wolof under Zebulun, and more. How do we know? By traveling: the bishops and brothers that travel went into the history of the people, and the Lord guided us. The chart is going to keep getting updated as the spirit reveals more.

note.label: Judgement! To Hell with Your Reparations!

precepts.why:
“Hear, Lord, the voice of Judah, and bring him unto his people”. There is Judah in Africa too, but this is speaking of Judah on this side of the earth, in the Western Hemisphere, specifically in the United States of America. Judah in North America is under Esau, who controls the world right now, and with an American passport you can go anywhere in the world. A Jamaican, Haitian or Nigerian passport cannot take you everywhere. That is why we tell you brothers: get your passport.

“The Lord also shall save the tents of Judah first”. God is going to raise up the tribe of Judah first, Judah in America. Then, when it says bring him unto his people, it means Judah will know where God's people are and will go find them. Wherever our people are in Africa, in Japan, in Iran, in India, scattered throughout the four corners of the earth, Judah will be able to identify them, find them, and teach them what God commanded of them.

That is why Genesis 49 speaks mainly of Israel on this side of the world: Judah needed to know who they were first. And it is already happening. The bishops and brothers that travel went into the history of the people, and they found Judah among the Igbo of Nigeria and the tribes scattered across Africa, India and the islands, now written on the revised twelve tribe chart. When people ask how we know, it is because the Lord showed us; the spirit guided us. That is “be thou an help to him from his enemies”: God is a help to Judah, making us find things so we are not guessing, and the chart will keep being updated as the Lord reveals more.

precepts.text: The controversy of Zion: Jerusalem a burdensome stone to all that burden themselves with it, and the Israelis holding and expanding a land that does not belong to them are being cut in pieces by it.
precepts.point: The Lord hath a sacrifice in Bozrah, the capital of Edom, and a great slaughter in the land of Idumea, the land of Israel today; their land soaked with blood, for it is the day of the Lord's vengeance and the year of recompenses for the controversy of Zion.

note.label: Edom: The Robbers of thy people revealed past and present

precepts.why:
“For the Lord hath a sacrifice in Bozrah, and a great slaughter in the land of Idumea.” Bozrah was the capital of Edom, and the land of Idumea is the land of Israel today, the Middle East, the Near East. “Their land shall be soaked with blood” … “For it is the day of the Lord’s vengeance, and the year of recompences for the controversy of Zion.” What is the controversy of Zion? Zechariah answers.

“And in that day will I make Jerusalem a burdensome stone for all people: all that burden themselves with it shall be cut in pieces, though all the people of the earth be gathered together against it.” God makes Jerusalem a burdensome stone to whoever holds it. These Israelis are trying to hold on to that land and spread it and expand it as much as they can, but it is becoming a burdensome stone to them, because they are not the chosen people of God and it doesn't belong to them.

Zechariah 14 shows it: all nations gathered against Jerusalem, the city taken, and then the Lord goes forth to fight and his feet stand on the Mount of Olives, and after that “there shall be no more utter destruction; but Jerusalem shall be safely inhabited.” Isaiah 60 says “Violence shall no more be heard in thy land” and “Thy people also shall be all righteous.” Ezekiel 38 says they “shall dwell safely all of them”, without walls, bars or gates.

Are the Israelis dwelling safely right now? No. They are in unsanitary bomb shelters, running and hiding and crying, behind walls. Where is their God at? The Messiah must return for us to get into the land, not before. That is why they are getting blown to hell over there: they don't belong there, and Jerusalem is cutting them in pieces.

precepts.text: The Lord saves the tents of Judah first; he that is feeble shall be as David, and the house of David, the 144,000, as God, as the angel of the Lord before them.
precepts.point: The whirlwind of the Lord goeth forth with fury and falls upon the head of the wicked, and the fierce anger of the Lord shall not return until he hath performed the intents of his heart; in the latter days ye shall consider it.

note.label: From Exile & Tribulation to Promise

precepts.why:
“The Lord also shall save the tents of Judah first, that the glory of the house of David and the glory of the inhabitants of Jerusalem do not magnify themselves against Judah.” These are the same tents of Jacob that the Lord brings again out of captivity.

“In that day shall the Lord defend the inhabitants of Jerusalem; and he that is feeble among them at that day shall be as David”. The feeble Israelites are going to be like King David. “and the house of David shall be as God, as the angel of the Lord before them.” The house of David is the 144,000; they shall be as God.

That is our children being as aforetime and our glorious state being restored: the Lord saving Judah’s tents first, and the weakest of Israel made as strong as David.

precepts.text: The Lord shall save the tents of Judah first. Romans 1:16 and 2:9 say the same: to the Jew first, and also to the Greek.
precepts.point: If the casting away of them be the reconciling of the world: reconcile means bringing back together what was together before, and the nations were never together with us. Isaiah 45:17 calls Israel the world without end, and Mark 10:30 speaks of the world to come. The receiving of them will be life from the dead, as Ephesians 2:1 says of those dead in trespasses and sins.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: the Grafted in Strangers

precepts.why:
Romans 11:11 says the leaders' fall brought salvation to the Gentiles “for to provoke them to jealousy”, as Moses said: “I will provoke you to jealousy by them that are no people”. The ones provoked are the southern kingdom, and the ones who are no people are the northern kingdom, who received Christ. But the southern kingdom still comes first.

“The Lord also shall save the tents of Judah first, that the glory of the house of David and the glory of the inhabitants of Jerusalem do not magnify themselves against Judah.” He will raise the tents of Judah first.

Paul says it too: the gospel of Christ “is the power of God unto salvation to every one that believeth; to the Jew first, and also to the Greek.” The Jew is Judah, first; the Greek is the northern kingdom. And judgment runs in the same order: “Tribulation and anguish, upon every soul of man that doeth evil, of the Jew first, and also of the Gentile”.

That is why Romans 11 says God has not cast away his people. Judah stumbled, but Judah is saved first, and the northern kingdom that received Christ provokes them to jealousy until they come in.

precepts.text: The Lord shall save the tents of Judah first, that the glory of the house of David do not magnify itself against Judah.
precepts.point: His eyes shall be red with wine: Christ drank wine, so much that men called him a winebibber, but he was never drunken.

note.label: Genesis 49: What Shall Befall the Twelve Tribes in the Last Days

precepts.why:
“The Lord also shall save the tents of Judah first, that the glory of the house of David and the glory of the inhabitants of Jerusalem do not magnify themselves against Judah.” The Lord saves the tents of Judah first. That is “thy father’s children shall bow down before thee”: Judah, the so-called American Black man today, is the top tribe in the awakening.

Judah was the first to bring out this truth that we are the nation of Israel, and the great majority of the teachers of this truth today are of the kingdom of Judah. “Judah, thou art he whom thy brethren shall praise.”

precepts.text: The Lord shall save the tents of Judah first; that word is in effect, and the lesson of the war between the kingdoms is to stand down when it comes to Judah.
precepts.point: Salt is a preservative; it keeps a thing fresh. The covenant of salt goes into the brotherhood: we are supposed to preserve our relationships, keep our alliance fresh, and grow together. Everything given to the Levites for sacrifice carried that symbolism.

note.label: Leviticus 2: The Meat Offering of Fine Flour

precepts.why:
The kingdom was given to David and his sons by a covenant of salt, and that word is still in effect: “The Lord also shall save the tents of Judah first, that the glory of the house of David and the glory of the inhabitants of Jerusalem do not magnify themselves against Judah.”

The lesson of the war between the northern kingdom and the southern kingdom is to stand down when it comes to Judah. Jeroboam had twice the men and it did not matter; the covenant of salt with David was preserved, and the Lord saves the tents of Judah first.

precepts.text: The Lord also shall save the tents of Judah first.
precepts.point: That is why Judah is at the forefront of this work. The gates of hell will try to prevail against the quest to wake up the twelve tribes, but the Most High is a help to Judah from his enemies to fulfill that mission.

note.label: Deuteronomy 33: The Blessing of Moses, Identifying the Tribes in the Last Days

precepts.why:
“Hear, Lord, the voice of Judah, and bring him unto his people: let his hands be sufficient for him; and be thou an help to him from his enemies.” The Most High said we would be scattered into the four corners and the nations would conspire that we not remember who we are. But he wakes Judah first: “The Lord also shall save the tents of Judah first”.

Judah, the so-called blacks in America, are the first to remember that they are the Israelites. Once Judah learns who they are, they go and teach the other tribes scattered throughout the four corners: that is bring him unto his people. That is why Judah is at the forefront of this work. The gates of hell will try to prevail against the quest to wake up the twelve tribes, but the Most High is an help to Judah from his enemies to fulfill that mission.

precepts.text: The Lord shall save the tents of Judah first, that the inhabitants of Jerusalem, which were Benjamin and Levi in there with Judah, do not magnify themselves against Judah. That is why you see so many of Judah, Benjamin, and Levi in the truth right now, with the northern kingdom trickling in; the Most High gives the head tribes what is most important first, not worldly things but the truth of who they are, to raise up the twelve tribes of Jacob. And he that is feeble among them at that day shall be as David, and the house of David shall be as God: all twelve tribes, as the angel of the Lord before them.
precepts.point: The bows of the mighty men are broken, and they that stumbled are girded with strength. The Lord is prophesying through Hannah here.

note.label: 1 Samuel 2: By Him Actions Are Weighed

precepts.why:
The Lord is prophesying through Hannah: “The bows of the mighty men are broken, and they that stumbled are girded with strength.” Zechariah shows who that is.

“The Lord also shall save the tents of Judah first, that the glory of the house of David and the glory of the inhabitants of Jerusalem do not magnify themselves against Judah.” The inhabitants of Jerusalem were Benjamin and Levi, in there with Judah. That is why you see so many of Judah, Benjamin and Levi in the truth right now, with the northern kingdom trickling in. The Most High gives the head tribes what is most important first: not worldly things, but the truth of who they are, to raise up the twelve tribes of Jacob.

Then: “and he that is feeble among them at that day shall be as David; and the house of David shall be as God, as the angel of the Lord before them.” That is all twelve tribes. He that is feeble shall be as David goes right back to “they that stumbled are girded with strength”: that is the house of Israel.

precepts.text: In that day He pours the spirit of grace upon the house of David, and every family mourns apart, which is the shame that comes upon us when the remembrance of our wickedness returns.
precepts.point: When He is pacified, she shall remember her ways, be ashamed, and never open her mouth anymore because of her shame, and she shall know that He is the Lord.

note.label: Ezekiel 16: The Harlot Redeemed by an Everlasting Covenant

precepts.why:
When He establishes His covenant, “Then thou shalt remember thy ways, and be ashamed”, and “never open thy mouth any more because of thy shame”. Zechariah shows what that day looks like. “In that day” the Most High seeks to destroy all the nations that come against Jerusalem, and pours “upon the house of David, and upon the inhabitants of Jerusalem, the spirit of grace and of supplications”.

Then “they shall look upon me whom they have pierced, and they shall mourn for him, as one mourneth for his only son”. There is “a great mourning in Jerusalem”, and the land mourns “every family apart”: the house of David apart, the house of Nathan apart, the house of Levi apart, the house of Shimei apart, all the families that remain, every family apart, and their wives apart.

That mourning is the shame that comes upon us when the remembrance of our wickedness returns. When He is pacified toward us for all we have done, and we remember our ways, we are confounded and never open our mouth any more. The spirit of grace and the shame come together, on His people, in that day.

precepts.text: "The LORD also shall save the tents of Judah first," showing the order in which the tribes are redeemed.
precepts.point: There was an order and prophecy for the twelve tribes to be redeemed. The gospel went first to the southern kingdom, Judah, Benjamin, and Levi, the "Jews," and the "Jew and Gentile" and "Jew and Greek" language is the split between the southern kingdom and the northern kingdom of Israel, not Israel and the nations. The Most High did not cast away the northern tribes; the whole twelve tribes are scattered and being saved.

note.label: Acts 3: The Restitution of All Things

precepts.why:
Unto you first means unto Judah, the Jews first. “The Lord also shall save the tents of Judah first, that the glory of the house of David and the glory of the inhabitants of Jerusalem do not magnify themselves against Judah.”

There was an order and a prophecy for the twelve tribes to be redeemed. The gospel went first to the southern kingdom, Judah, Benjamin and Levi, the Jews, and Peter is preaching to them.

precepts.text: The Most High saves the tents of Judah first, so Judah wakes up before the rest.
precepts.point: It says "the Jew first, and also the Gentile" because prophecy set Judah, Benjamin, and Levi to rise up first, and the "Gentiles" are the dispersed northern tribes scattered among the heathen, left few in number. This is the diaspora, the same scattering some now call the African diaspora.

note.label: Acts 10: Cornelius and the Northern Kingdom Grafted In

precepts.why:
“The Lord also shall save the tents of Judah first, that the glory of the house of David and the glory of the inhabitants of Jerusalem do not magnify themselves against Judah.”

That is why it is “the Jew first.” The Most High saves the tents of Judah first, so Judah wakes up before the rest. Then come the Gentiles, the northern tribes.

precepts.text: The Lord shall save the tents of Judah first, that the house of David not magnify itself against Judah.
precepts.point: The reason they preached to the Jews only is the prophecy that the Most High saves the tents of Judah first.

note.label: Acts 11: The Gentiles Are Scattered Israel

precepts.why:
“Now they which were scattered abroad upon the persecution that arose about Stephen travelled as far as Phenice, and Cyprus, and Antioch, preaching the word to none but unto the Jews only.” They went where the Israelites were scattered. Phenice was the coastal region north of Israel, modern Lebanon; Cyprus is an island in the eastern Mediterranean; Antioch was a major Roman city in ancient Syria, now Antakya, Turkey.

They preached to the Jews only because of the prophecy: “The Lord also shall save the tents of Judah first, that the glory of the house of David and the glory of the inhabitants of Jerusalem do not magnify themselves against Judah.” The Most High saves the tents of Judah first.

Then some of them, “men of Cyprus and Cyrene”, came to Antioch and “spake unto the Grecians, preaching the Lord Jesus.” Those Grecians, or Hellenists, were Greek-speaking Jews. The Holman Christian Standard Bible calls them Hellenists, and the Zondervan compact Bible dictionary defines a Hellenist as a Jew who made Greek his tongue and adopted Greek ideas and practices.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 8 A Star Called Wormwood

precepts.why:
The Lord will plead with us face to face; here is the precept, where he shows us his hands. “And it shall come to pass in that day, that I will seek to destroy all the nations that come against Jerusalem. And I will pour upon the house of David, and upon the inhabitants of Jerusalem, the spirit of grace and of supplications:” Grace is only for the house of David, the twelve tribes of Israel. You have these Christians running around talking about grace is for everybody; no, it is not, not according to the Bible.

“and they shall look upon me whom they have pierced,” That is the evidence: Christ is going to be in our midst, walking amongst us, the tallest of us all, the greatest of us all. “and they shall mourn for him, as one mourneth for his only son,” When we see him we are going to cry on that day, all of us, man, woman, boy, everybody, because the spirit is going to move us. “and shall be in bitterness for him, as one that is in bitterness for his firstborn.” As if your firstborn dies: if anyone's child dies, you know that feeling in you; some of us don't know what that is like, but some do. On this day all of us are going to feel like that when we see Christ and he shows us what was done to him. We are going to cry bitterly on that day.
